title: The VLT goes lion hunting
caption: The spiral galaxy Messier 95, imaged by ESO's Very Large Telescope
celestial: Messier 95 · constellation Leo · about 35 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Messier 95 faces us almost head-on, its spiral arms forming a nearly perfect circle around the centre before spreading out like a lion's mane. At the heart of the galaxy glows a bright golden core. The Very Large Telescope captured this galaxy, one of the Leo I group, in the constellation Leo, the Lion.

That core contains a star-forming ring almost 2000 light-years across, where much of the galaxy's star birth takes place. Such rings appear mostly in barred spiral galaxies, a class that includes both Messier 95 and the Milky Way.

Messier 96, the brightest member of the Leo I group, outshines Messier 95 and gives the group its other name, the M 96 group. Around the time this picture was released, Messier 95 became host to a probable supernova, first spotted on 17 March 2012. The observations were made before the explosion, so it is not in the image.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (6.80 x 6.81 arcminutes) and distance (35 million light years), the frame spans roughly 69,000 × 69,000 light-years. Its light set out about 35 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: FORS1 on the Very Large Telescope observed Messier 95 in visible and near-infrared light through V and I filters, with a synthetic green channel. The colour assigned to each filter isn't published.
understand.eye: The near-infrared light is invisible to the eye, and the telescope's exposures gather far more light than an eye can.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: At the time of release, both the galaxy and the supernova sat close to the planet Mars among the stars of Leo, according to ESO. The image was made with the FORS1 instrument through V and I filters.
alt: A face-on spiral galaxy with a golden core and a ring of arms spreading outwards.
